misconceptions.description: Reporting AI use with a vague blanket statement that names neither what the AI did nor how the human verified it
misconceptions.trigger: disclosure says only that AI was used somewhere, with no decision, location, or verification
misconceptions.feedback: Name what the AI produced, where, and how you checked it. A blanket line is not an honest account.

misconceptions.description: Framing AI-generated content as objective or authoritative to shift accountability away from the designer
misconceptions.trigger: disclosure presents AI output as inherently neutral, so the human is no longer answerable for it
misconceptions.feedback: Keep accountability with the designer. AI output is a draft you verified, not an objective authority.

misconceptions.description: Assuming disclosure can be skipped if the work is mostly human, or if the AI draft was later edited
misconceptions.trigger: learner omits disclosure because they polished the wording or judge their contribution as dominant
misconceptions.feedback: Provenance follows the contribution, not the final wording. Disclose the bounded decision the AI supported even after you edit it.
